name: Fetal Valproate Spectrum Disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Fetal Valproate Spectrum Disorder

criteria.description: Confirmed prenatal exposure to valproate during pregnancy
Characteristic facial features including broad nasal bridge, epicanthic folds, and thin upper lip
Presence of congenital malformations such as neural tube defects or cardiac anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Confirmed prenatal valproate exposure plus presence of characteristic facial dysmorphism and neurodevelopmental impairment
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing may be used to exclude other syndromes.

laboratory: Normal metabolic and hematologic studies; no specific laboratory biomarker
imaging: Prenatal or postnatal ultrasound showing neural tube defects
MRI brain may show structural abnormalities
genetic: No specific genetic mutation; diagnosis based on teratogenic exposure history
other: Detailed maternal medication history critical for diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Distinctive facial features different from valproate syndrome

redFlags: Confirmed prenatal valproate exposure with neurodevelopmental delay
Presence of neural tube defects in neonate
Characteristic facial dysmorphism in infant with developmental concerns
references: Tomson T, et al. Valproate in pregnancy: risks and recommendations. Epilepsia. 2011.
Meador KJ, et al. Fetal antiepileptic drug exposure and cognitive outcomes at age 6 years. Neurology. 2013.
